name: active-ring-unload
summary: Unload Sample while a frost dash ring is still inside its log-time lifetime. A FROSTDASH cleanup line with alive>=1 and the tracked ring in destroyed is the disposal proof; an exists readback after removal alone cannot distinguish disposal from expiry.
notes: Acceptance procedure. With a Sample image that logs exactly one line `FROSTDASH cleanup alive=<n> destroyed=[<index:version>,...]` at unload and at `.frostdash off` (alive=0 destroyed=[] when nothing was alive), this case completes as a disposal proof: unload destroyed a ring that was alive. Without that line (older Sample image) the log step fails and the case stays aborted.

The ring lives ~1.5 s. Removal waits for the reloader's full unload (~3.3 s live). existsAt after that wait therefore cannot tell disposal from expiry on its own: live catalog-cases-3 saw Start 09:32:23.674, unload 09:32:23.969 (log delta 295 ms), wall ageMs 3318, exists false.

What this case can show: (a) the cleanup line names a live ring (alive>=1 and the tracked id as a whole token in destroyed=[...], not a substring of another id), recorded as ringUnloadCleanup; (b) logAgeMs from the FROSTDASH Start line to the Progenitor.Sample.dll removed line is under 1500 (existsAt after that line, ageClock log, maxAgeMs 1500); (c) existsAt of the ring is then false.

Flow: .frostdash on, .frostdash dash, logEntity(ring) from edge=Start, existsAt ring expect true, removal, log FROSTDASH cleanup alive= since ringLog (regex with @tracked:ring, alive>=1) recorded as ringUnloadCleanup, existsAt after the unload line with ageClock log / maxAgeMs 1500 / expect any, existsAt ring expect false. .frostdash off is teardown so it still runs after abort. Before that command, a leftover .rig-hold is restored (report.teardown.restore) so Sample is loaded to handle off; expectLog requires the Sample line `FROSTDASH cleanup alive=` from ClearRings. A missing handler line fails teardown and the run is incomplete.

The ring is adopted from the log, not spawned by the rig. It is not hostile and is not destroyed on cleanup unless track is true. A leftover .rig-hold after removal is put back before teardown (and again by the run fail-safe if it remains) so final protection can be checked. That restore is not the observation.
